text: J. Shoesteer is a character in Cars. He is a supporter of Rust-eze, a medicated bumper ointment trademark that sponsors rookie race car Lightning McQueen.
J. Low Lee is a Piston Cup fan who supports Strip Weathers. He is a small car with a blue livery and chrome rims.
J.P. Drive is a Next-gen racer that races for Apple, Inc. and bearings the number 84. He has replaced the Apple stock-car racer in the 2016 mid-season.
Gale Gourtney was a crew member for Pixar Animation Studios. They served as the producer for Mike's New Car and Exploring the Reef.
Johnny Blamer is a Faux Wheel Drive race car and is one of the characters in Cars.
Jerry Recycled Batteries (credited as Peterbilt) is a minor character in Cars. He is the truck that was thought to be Mack by Lightning McQueen. He is a truck who does a few deliveries at night.
Kabuto is a main character in the Cars Toons episode Tokyo Mater. He is a Japanese drift racer that Mater races against. He also makes a cameo appearance in Cars 2.

John Walker (born April 21, 1956) is an American film producer. He served as producer on The Iron Giant (1999), Pixar's The Incredibles and Incredibles 2. He was scheduled to produce The Good Dinosaur but was removed from the project and Denise Ream took role as the producer, however, he was credited for additional production leadership. He is married to actress Pamela Gayle Walker who provided additional voices in The Incredibles.
Japeth is a rusty car that uses Rust-eze and supports Lightning McQueen.
Kim Carllins is a television host that works for MPH 55 News, along with Dan Sclarkenberg. Carllins is a small car that is painted dark blue. She has chrome rims.
Jim Reverick is a Piston Cup race car who appears in Cars 3.
Jan Mybrand is the Swedish voice of Woody in Buzz Lightyear of Star Command: The Adventure Begins and beyond and does the Swedish voice for Woody Car in Cars
Jonathan Shiftko is an Italian car who can be seen watching the second WGP race in Porto Corsa, Italy.
The Lavatory Services truck is an unnamed character that was seen collecting waster from a plane, but not before Acer falling into it and was shocked.

Jeremy Charles Robert Clarkson (born April 11, 1960) is an English broadcaster, TV personality, journalist and writer, well known for hosting the UK car show Top Gear from 2002 until 2015, when he was dropped out after verbally and physically attacking the show's producer in a hotel over a dispute. He voiced Harv in the UK version of Cars.

John Cygan (April 27, 1954 - May 13, 2017) provided additional voices for Cars, Green Hawk and Stinky the Garbage Truck in the Cars Toons: Mater's Tall Tales episodes Air Mater and Mater Private Eye, Twitch in Toy Story 3, Idle Threat in The Radiator Springs 500½, and Roy "Big Red" O'Growlahan in Monsters University. He died on May 13, 2017 at the age of 63 due to cancer.

Jeffery Michael "Jeff" Gordon (born August 4, 1971) is an American professional stock car racing driver and currently an announcer for Fox NASCAR. He performed the voice of Jeff Gorvette in Cars 2 and Cars 3. ru:Гордон, Джефф
From 2011-2012, The LEGO Group has released 14 Cars and Cars 2-themed LEGO sets, as well as 8 Duplo sets, later it was replaced by LEGO Cars 3 for 2017 film Cars 3.

Jamie Metzger is a staff member at Pixar Animation Studios. Metzger graduated from the animation program at Sheridan College in April 2011. "Eight years of school, about $53,000 in tuition, 56 teachers, and no social life, and it all equals Pixar", she says of her path to the studio, but she adds that it will be worth it. Metzger finally started work at Pixar as an animation intern from June to August 2011. She is now working in Animation instruction and implementation.

Mike's New Car is a 2002 Pixar animated short, starring the two main characters from Monsters, Inc., Mike Wazowski and James P. Sullivan. Directed by Pete Docter and Roger Gould, it is the first Pixar short to utilize vocal performances and the first to take characters and situations from a previously established work. It received an Academy Award nomination (Best Animated Short Film in 2002) and was included in the 2002 VHS and DVD release of Monsters, Inc. It was also released theatrically with a non-Pixar Animation Studios feature, Treasure Planet (made by Walt Disney Pictures), on November 27, 2002.
The Little Red Car is a toy that appeared in Toy Story 2. It is driven by the Shriner Tike.
Memo Rojas, Jr. is a character that appears in the Latin Spanish dub of Cars 2. He is a race car that Lightning McQueen meets at the World Grand Prix welcome party.
Long Ge is a character who appears in the Chinese version of Cars 2. He is a race car whom Lightning McQueen meets at the World Grand Prix welcome party.
Mater Goes to the Car-Nival was set to be an episode of Cars Toons, but it was canceled.

Mike Lorengine is a character in Cars 2. He is a black Land Rover Range Rover and a bodyguard of the Queen. Like all other bodyguards, he is equipped with a gun concealed in his wheel. When Mater lands on the Queen's platform, the bodyguards quickly realize he has a bomb implanted on him. They interpose themselves between him and the Queen, thinking he wants to attack her. He is named after Michael Lorenzen, who was the crowds technical supervisor for Cars 2 and the crowds lead for Cars 1.

M.A. Brake Drumm is a car that is a fan of the Piston Cup Racing Series. In Cars, M.A. can be seen on Los Angeles International Speedway. She, Brake Boyd, and Coriander Widetrack watch admiringly as Marco, Stu Bop, and another jet fly over them.
Michael Sparkber is a rusty car that uses and supports Rust-eze, the bumper ointment product that sponsors Piston Cup race car Lightning McQueen.
Max Sacar is a fan of the Japanese race car Shu Todoroki, who competes in the World Grand Prixalongside ten other international champions.

"Oliver likes posing as a long-haul trucker, but the truth is he just likes the Top Down Truck Stop. You see, he's actually an online stockbroker, and he lives less than a mile down the road. He likes to pop in once in a while and crack some jokes, take a nap, or just listen to stories from the constantly changing clientele, all on their way to someplace far off and exotic."
Monster Truck Mater is the sixth short in the Cars Toons series.

The National Automotive Space Car Association (NASCA for short) is an agency responsible for space exploration that appears in the Cars Toons short Moon Mater. In the episode, it is the agency that Mater trains/works for to save autonaut Impala XIII from the moon.

Mount Wannahockaloogie is the volcano inside of Philip Sherman's office fish tank in Finding Nemo. Its name is pronounced as "Mount Wanna-hock-a-loogie" (a "loogie" is a slang term for a lump of phlegm, so it literally means "want to hock a loogie").

Philip Sherman's office fish tank is the fish tank owned by the dentist Philip Sherman located in his office in Sydney, Australia. It is one of the main locations in Finding Nemo. The fish tank contains various fake corals and seaweeds, a bubble-blowing treasure chest (Bubbles' favorite toy), a Tiki hut, a diving helmet (Jacques' hideout), a pirate skull (Gill's hideout), a trio of Tiki heads (based on the producers of the film), a "Didn't Brush" sign and barrel, a pirate ship (which has the Sunny Atlantis mermaid from Knick Knack as a figurehead), and a "swimming" scuba diver puppet.

Pathway nodes are electronic pathways in WALL•E, used to direct bots and human passengers around the ship. If a passenger falls out of his/her chair, or a bot steps out of line, the node flashes and makes a beeping noise. bots, GO-4 and the cleaning crew wait on pathway nodes. ]]The reject bots do not seem to follow the pathways, and as humans were still meant to walk around the ship, the pathway nodes couldn't control them either. contemplates whether he should follow WALL-E off the pathway. ]]
Patrick Walker voiced Mel Dorado in Cars 2. He was also one of the additional voices in The Incredibles.
John Walker (simply known as "Principal") is a minor character in The Incredibles. He is the principal of Metroville Elementary School.

Ryan Shields races for the team "View Zeen" in the movie Cars. He appears to be a turquoise car with robin's egg blue overlays on the windows and the spoiler, the eye color of sky blue, and the maize number 39. "Ryan is not only a View Zeen Corrective Windshields driver, he's also a customer. Without it, the race is merely a blur of multi-colored blobs moving at 200 miles per hour. His View Zeen windshield doesn't just help out on the track, it also has a special coating that helps cut down on glare while driving at night, not to mention it makes him look smarter."

The Pickup Truck is a toy who appears in Toy Story. It is a broken, sand-covered red pickup truck with a dented hood and roof, a crooked bumper, and a severely-fractured windshield. The model of the Pickup Truck is a [https://automobile.fandom.com/wiki/Toyota_Hilux Toyota Hilux].

Roger Gould is a director and former chief creative officer at Pixar. He has worked on several Pixar film and has directed two short films: Mike's New Car and Boundin. Besides working at Pixar, Roger is also a creative officer at Walt Disney Animation Studios and a principal advisor for Walt Disney Imagineering.
Reb Meeker is a character in Cars 3. He is a race car that formerly competed in the Piston Cup Racing Series for the Tank Coat racing team with the number 36. He was replaced by Rich Mixon.
Rex Revler is a race car who races for the team "Gask-Its" in the movie Cars 3.
Rev Roadages is a character in Cars 3. He is a stock-car racer who raced for Vinyl Toupee. He later retired from the Piston Cup, and got replaced by Will Rusch.

Pushover is a character that appears in Cars 3. He is a demolition derby car who competes at the Crazy Eight. His number is 16. He is painted orange with yellow stripes, and has a "mouth" painted on his sides, and a white bumper. He is sponsored by "This-N-That".

Raymond Francis Magliozzi (born March 30, 1949) was one of the co-hosts of NPR's weekly radio show Car Talk alongside his brother Tom, where they were known as "Click and Clack, the Tappet Brothers." Their show was honored with a Peabody Award in 1992. Ray voiced Dusty Rust-eze in Cars and Cars 3.
Snot Rod is a supporting character in Cars. He is also a muscle car who suffers from severe allergies and a member of the Import Racers.
Stephenson is a character in Cars 2. He is a spy train who works with Finn McMissile.

Taia Decotura, the Tire Talky truck, is a cameo character in Cars 2. "Taia used to be an ordinary, gray truck in the muffler transport business, working the Sawara-to-Tokyo line. But he dreamed of more exciting things than peddling parts, so he moved to Tokyo to get into advertising. Now, painted in a shiny yellow and purple, with stainless trim and two gigantic TV screens, Taia certainly attracts attention. In fact, he's the most popular truck in town - he can turn any boring party into a drive-in movie with the flip of a switch!" He gets through the streets of Tokyo, equipped with a large screen that airs the Tire Talky show. He is seen when Lightning McQueen and Mater are cruising in Tokyo. At that moment, the show was featuring Francesco Bernoulli demonstrating his talents in soccer.
Suki is a small drift car that appears in Tokyo Mater and Cars 2.

Subway is an American fast-food restaurant franchise that sells submarine sandwiches and salads. It is owned and operated by Doctor's Associates, Inc., and one of the fastest growing franchises in the world.

"TRUCKS" is a song heard in the Disney/Pixar Disney+ series, Cars on the Road, and featured in the episode of the same name. The song is essentially a truck's appreciation number involving Mater as he meets numerous trucks that sing and show him about why it is great to be a truck.

is the Noble Phantasm of Arjuna. It is a Bow of Flames that essentially cannot be handled by humans (mortals), awarded to Arjuna by the Flame God, Agni. Normally just a regular bow, by activating its True Name, its arrow becomes a missile engulfed in flames. It is not a homing missile, but since Arjuna is an archery genius and possesses the Clairvoyance Skill, its precision is that of a homing missile anyway.
The is an unnamed Angel A-Ray acquainted with Gun God in Notes.

is the name of the Divine Construct spear of creation once held by the deities Izanagi and Izanami. It was used to create the islands of Japan. EMIYA Alter notes that if anyone were to possess the original Amenonuboko it’d have to be a high-ranking Divine Spirit.
is a Mana Conversion Engine that serves as the heart of an Anti-Anti Saber Decisive Weapon. The Alternium embedded within converts calories into magical energy.

is the Noble Phantasm of Taira-no-Kagekiyo. A cursed attack slammed at the enemy with a sword engulfed in the grudges of the Taira-clan. There is no universal or everlasting in this world, be it an immortal warrior or an eternal nation───────turning such providence into a blade, the target is shaved off along with its existence. Perhaps due to the anecdote of her being a wielder of a large long sword having been sublimated, along with the release of the Noble Phantasm's True Name, her weapon transforms from the dual Azamaru swords into a single enormous blade. It can be understood by those other than the Genji, but as expected, it will only be fully comprehended by the Genji.

is the Great Noble Phantasm of Yamato Takeru. A divine sword created in the myth of Susanoo and wielded by the legendary Yamato Takeru. It was brought forth from the tail of the eight-headed, red-eyed beast known as Japan's most fearsome Dragon of Destruction, Yamata-no-Orochi. That is to say, it is an embodiment of the various powers, both of heaven and earth, that were contained within the Dragon's body. To use this Noble Phantasm is to momentarily become a god or, in other words, to become one with the world. This is where its True Name, Sword of Heaven: Amenomurakumo-no-Tsurugi, is derived. It is a type of Divine Construct. An ARM is the weapon used by the playable characters in ARMS. Toaster - These arms catch fire when charged up. They will knock down the enemy and set the enemy on fire. Megaton - These arms are slow but they are large and do heavy damage. When charged, the Megaton will become bigger and are able to block and push away enemy punch attacks. Sparky - Sparky arms are charged with electricity. They will shock and stun the opponent when charged up. Boomerang - These arms are able to arc around obstacles for a sneak attack.
A fighter is a playable character in ARMS. There are fifteen available fighters, with ten releasing in the game's initial launch, and five added as free-DLC fighters later on.

The Scorpio arms resemble scorpions. They can poison any opponent they hit. The Scorpio is also known for being a "cute" weapon in the description. The Scorpio, when fully charged after guarding, this weapon will also again, poison the opponent it hits. Appearance: Green, red and purple. The eyes are purple and the body is green. A lined circle is red. It scuttles when launched. Works well with: Misango

Baki Gaiden: Kenjin (バキ外伝 拳刃, Baki Gaiden Kenjin; literally: "Baki's Side Story: Blade Fist") is a spinoff series, written by Keisuke Itagaki and illustrated by Kenko Miyatani, representing and describing Doppo's adventures. Began in Champion Red in June 2013, currently 1 volume.

Grappler Baki (グラップラー刃牙, Gurappurā Baki), known as Grappler Baki: The Ultimate Fighter in the English version, is a 45-minute original video animation (OVA) was released in 1994. The story is a close adaptation of the first few volumes of the original manga, in which Baki Hanma fights Shinogi Koushou. It was licensed and released on VHS and DVD, under the title Baki The Grappler: The Ultimate Fighter, in North America by Central Park Media on VHS in February 1997, and DVD on December 1, 1998. Manga Entertainment later released it in Australia and the United Kingdom.
Baki Against the Japanese Blade (日本刀VS刃牙) is a chapter of the Baki the Grappler manga series.
A True Fighter (正ファイター) is a chapter of the Baki the Grappler manga series.

Anime may refer to: *Baki The Grappler: The Ultimate Fighter, OVA released in 1994. *Baki The Grappler TV, first anime series aired on TV Tokyo from January 8, 2001 to June 25, 2001. *Baki The Grappler: Maximum Tournament, second anime series aired on TV Tokyo from July 23, 2001 to December 24, 2001. *Baki (2018 ONA), third anime series aired on Tokyo MX1 from June 25, 2018 to December 16, 2018. *Baki (2020 ONA), fourth anime series aired on Netflix on June 4, 2020. *Hanma Baki (2021 ONA), fifth anime series aired on Netflix on September 30, 2021. *Hanma Baki (2023 ONA), sixth anime series aired on Netflix, with two parts released on July 26, 2023 and August 24, 2023. *Baki-Dou (ONA), seventh anime series aired on Netflix, with two parts released on February 26, 2026 and June 18, 2026.
The Ultimate Weapon!! (最終兵器!!) is the twenty-fifth chapter of Baki the Grappler manga series.
Righteousness and Sword (義と剣) is the 167th chapter of Baki-Dou.
Real Sword is the sixth episode of Baki-Dou (ONA) anime series.
Practical Fighter is the thirteenth episode of Baki-Dou (ONA) anime series.
The Scar and the Sword is the twenty-first episode of the Baki-Dou (ONA) anime series.
Yuujirou Versus the Bow (豪弓VS勇次郎) is a chapter of the Baki the Grappler manga series.

Battlestars were a class of armored battleship/carrier hybrids in service in the Colonial Fleet. They emerged during the Cylon War as a solution to Cylon hacking, which had destroyed numerous cruisers. The first battlestars were specifically designed to use primitive, unnetworked computers that could not be hacked. Further, they were armored to withstand nuclear blasts and carried dozens to hundreds of Vipers to defend their anti-ship weaponry. By the time of the Fall of the Twelve Colonies, the Colonial Fleet had approximately 120 battlestars in service divided into battlestar groups.

Type-D Basestar, also known as Modern Basestar or Baseship was the primary capital ship used by the Cylons at the time of the Fall of the Twelve Colonies and ensuing Second Cylon War. They performed an similar role to the Colonial Fleet's battlestars, that of being armoured fleet carriers/battleship hybrids.
Adriatic was a Defender-class ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies with The Fleet. It was destroyed two years after the fall, several weeks following the exodus from New Caprica.
An Air Group is a formation of small military spacecraft coordinated by a larger capital ship, usually a battlestar. Its most senior officer has the designation of Commander, Air Group or "CAG".

Alert Vipers is a group of Vipers onboard a Colonial warship that are fueled, armed, and immediately ready to the start. They are separate from the Vipers flying CAP (Combat Air Patrol). Pilots for the Alert Vipers are presumably already seated in the planes or close by on the hangar deck. They serve as a backup for the CAP and as a stopgap before the full complement can be mobilized.
Argo Navis was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as part of a refugee fleet. Its captain was selected to be a judge at Baltar's trial.
Azimenarius was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.

Baah Pakal was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election. This ship also had pair of unused DDG-62 engines, which were later used by Blackbird.
Amduatey was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as part of a refugee fleet.
Aether was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as part of the ragtag fleet.
Adrasteia was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as part of the ragtag fleet.

"BREAKING: MLMT Train Explosion; Casualties Estimated in the Hundreds" is the title of a blog entry published on syfy.com. Part of "The Caprican", it is written in an in-universe style to explain the backstory of Caprica.
Alex Hyde-White is a British actor known for playing the role of "Cadet Bow" in the Battlestar Galactica 1978 series.

Type-A Basestar was a type of warship utilized by the 12 Colonies before the First Cylon War, and the Cylons during the First Cylon War. Visually, the basestar appeared as center-joined two flattened cones giving it a distinctive saucer-like appearance. Similar to the modern Type-D, the primary armament was multiple missile launchers dotted alongside the circular hull. Hangar bays were located in the central hull at the end of one of the 10 trenches.

The Alert-type escort ship was a type of purpose-built warship utilized by the Colonial Fleet during the First Cylon War. Sister class of the Hornet-type, these once mighty Colonial ships are not delegated to serve as escorts to the newly built battlestars of Jupiter-class. By the tenth year of the war, at least one vessel of this class was retrofitted as a hospital ship.

Basestar Type-B was a type of warship utilized by the Cylons in the Cylon War. Deployed sometime before the 10th year of the war, this type of basestar was the first to feature the now-iconic "Y" design seen in later iterations mixed with the flattened-cone shape of Type A.

Type-C Basestar was a type of warship utilized by the Cylons in the closing years of the Cylon War. Visually, Type C closely resembles the Modern Basestar, albeit with a more industrial look, compared to the organic one of the latter type. It is the first known type that is controlled by a Hybrid, rather than conventional control.

Battlestar Galactica: Starship Battles is a miniature board game that was created by Ares Games and released in 2018. The starter set comes with two Vipers Mk. II and two Cylon Raiders along with their corresponding maneuver cards, a control panel, and a rotating miniature base. After the game was released, it received several scenarios and an expansion called "Faster Than Light". However, Ares Games' license for the game expired on December 31, 2021, and as a result, the game is no longer available for sale.

==Dev Diary # 1== Dev Diary -1 1.png Lore relevance: The image gives details about how commonly used the Adamant Cruiser was in the Twelve Colonies, and why the Adamant Cruiser was so successful. It also gives details about Sinon Quade's response to the Adamant's success.

Celestra was a starship that carried human refugees away from the Cyrannus Star System following the Fall of the Twelve Colonies. It was a deep space exploration vessel filled with scientific laboratories, research equipment and advanced sensor systems. It featured a long-range FTL drive for distant travel and was designed to function for years without resupply of fuel reserves and life support.

The Combat Information Center, or CIC, is the nerve center of a Colonial Fleet warship. Located deep inside the ship in the most well-protected area, the CIC is where all command functions are executed from. Inside the CIC you can find the Commander of the ship and his XO, usually the CAG could be found from the CIC too, but if the ship is experiencing lack of manpower the CAG might be flying with the other Viper or Raptor pilots.

The Commander, Air Group (CAG) is a senior officer aboard a Colonial Fleet ship, typically holding the rank of Captain or Major. The CAG oversees the ship’s Viper and Raptor squadrons, including pilots, spacecraft, flight operations, and training. They also play a key role in developing and advising on battle strategy.

Carina is a salvage and repairs flattop ship that was lost during the dangerous transit of a radiation filled star cluster. The ship escorted by Louanne "Kat" Katraine . Due to the extremely hazardous and low visibility conditions of the passage, the Carina was separated from it's escort and ultimately lost with all hands.

Chrion was a Gemenon Liner 1701-type civilian cruiser, that was part of The Fleet led by Battlestar Galactica following the Fall of the Twelve Colonies. People of Chiron participated in the presidential election with stated population of 591. The ship was later successfully guided by Captain Louanne "Kat" Katraine throughout the passage to the Algae planet. Chrion was last seen as one of the ships scuttled in the Sol System, roughly four years after the Fall.

Caprica Clipper was a Gemenon Liner 1701-type civilian cruiser, in service of Pan Galactic airline. The ship was first seen as part of President Roslin's fleet, before joining Battlestar Galactica at Ragnar Anchorage. Surviving through the Battle of New Caprica and the passage to the Algae planet, she was ultimately scuttled in the Sol System approximately four years after The Fall.

The Valkyrie (BS-41) was a Gen I Valkyrie-class battlestar in service in the Colonial Fleet. A relic of the Cylon War, the ship was continually upgraded to maintain usefulness in the fleet, and as part of BSG-41 saw action in classified operations as well as Caprican defense patrol. It was destroyed in the opening hours of the Fall of the Twelve Colonies.
Coba was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Cassandra was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Clymene was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Boreas was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.

Tankers are a class of starship used by the Cylon Empire for the transport of fuel and the refueling of vessels in interstellar transit. During the Battle of Cimtar, tankers were used in place of Basestars to refuel a massive Raider force, and were equipped with jamming technology.
Christine Belford is an American actress known for playing the role of Leda in the Battlestar Galactica 1978 two-parter, "The Gun on Ice Planet Zero".
Breton was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as part of a refugee fleet.
Carillon Trader was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as part of a refugee fleet.
The Caprica-class was type of support ship utilized by the Colonial Fleet during the interwar period shortly before the Fall of the Twelve Colonies.
The Civilian Raptor was a Mk. IIIb Raptor multipurpose spacecraft used by civilian population of the United Colonies of Kobol.
The Chronos-type battlestar was a type of warship utilized by the Colonial Fleet during the interwar period shortly before the Fall of the Twelve Colonies.
Cloud 9 Cruises is a cruiser operator company operating in the Twelve Colonies. They were the owners of the Cloud 9 luxury liner.
Colonial APC was an armored personnel carrier used by the Colonial Fleet, and more generally, the Colonial Marine Corps. This four-wheeled armored transport is equipped with a top-mounted turret.

The Core Command Center of any warship, such as a battlestar, was its Main Bridge, from which personnel who served there could monitor activity aboard such a warship itself or the activities of other warships or civilian ships where necessary.

Collishaw was a Colonial Marine who escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies onboard Galactica. Following the crash of a Heavy Raider into the ship's starboard flight pod, a number of Centurions stormed the ship.

An FTL, or "Faster Than Light", drive is a fictional propulsion technology from the re-imagined Battlestar Galactica series. It allows spacecraft to achieve faster-than-light travel. The verb jump is commonly used to describe the process of travelling via FTL drive. Dialogue states that the drive itself is "spooled up" prior to use. The term FTL is commonly used in the original Battlestar Galactica 1978 film and television series. The term FTL is also commonly used when the show is being discussed by outside parties.

Daru Mozu (Refinery 322) was a civilian refinery ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as part of a refugee fleet led by Galactica and Colonial One. A tylium processing vessel, the ship was crucial to the fleet's fuel supply. Several months after the Fall, terrorist group "Demand Peace" damaged the ship in a suicide bombing, killing four, though the damage was otherwise negligible. Sometime after, the Daru Mozu's refining facilities are destroyed, leaving Hitei Kan as the sole source of tylium for the fleet.

Freighter 212 was a civilian ship that survived the destruction of the Twelve Colonies of Kobol by the Cylons. It was the home vessel of Louanne "Kat" Katraine before she joined the Galactica Combat Air Group.

A large ship, yet still dwarfed by Galactica, the Gemini appears as a long container transport consisting of a central hull structure affixed with numerous external cargo pods of various livery design and nomenclature. During the miniseries, Gemini is originally part of Roslin's refugee fleet before joining the Battlestar Galactica A second Gemini freighter would be seen with it several times throughout the series after the Season 1 episode, Hand of God. The ship is a carry-over design of the Gemini, (an ordnance freighter), from the original series. The ship later survived the passage through the cluster to the Algae Planet
Gideon was a civilian cargo ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies by joining President Laura Roslin's refugee fleet under the protection of Galactica.

Delphi was a freighter which escaped the Cylon attack on the Twelve Colonies of Man and formed part of a civilian fleet led by Galactica. The ship was used predominantly as a place of education, and could carry a large number of children. Following the discovery of Earth and the fleet's departure from it, Delphi was sent back to land its children on the planet to keep them safe from the Cylons. During its journey back to Earth, it experienced engine trouble and got the attention of a Cylon patrol. A Viper squadron destroyed the attackers, but Delphi suffered serious damage and exploded seconds after its shuttles evacuated.

Inchon Velle was a ship that survived the Cylon holocaust and fleed the Cyrannus Star System in the ragtag fleet led by the Galactica. After Lieutenant Kara Thrace began to have disturbing dreams of the Cylon Leoben, Helo suggests she see a psychiatrist on the Inchon Velle, and after sustaining injuries, during the mutiny on board the Galactica a brain surgeon is brought from the Inchon Velle to help Samuel T. Anders.

Hexare was a civilian ship which survived the Fall of the Twelve Colonies, joining a refugee fleet led by Galactica. Refugees on the ship took part in the Presidential election almost a year after the Fall.
Galatea was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Epheme was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Enkidu was a civilian Astral Queen-type ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet.
Harrak was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Dashur was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Diomedes was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as part of a refugee fleet.

Gemini was a large Galactican cargo transport ship. Following the destruction of the Twelve Colonies of Man at the hands of the Cylon Empire, Gemini was launched over-capacity with refugees. Due to state of this emergency, Gemini was not in fact spaceworthy and required urgent maintenance to prevent a radiation leak. A team from Galactica was sent by Shuttle to assess the maintenance and evacuate seriously-wounded civilians.

Denny Miller was an American actor best known for his role as Duke Shannon in the 1957-1965 Western, Wagon Train. He was cast as the Male Thetas in the Battlestar Galactica 1978 two-parter, The Gun on Ice Planet Zero.
The Hornet-type was type of warship utilized by the Colonial Fleet during the First Cylon War.
Hitei Kan was a Daru Mozu-type refinery ship ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as part of a refugee fleet led by Galactica and Colonial One.

The Defender-class fleet escort was a type of warship utilized by the Colonial Fleet during the First Cylon War. At some point during its career, at least two of these ships were sold off to non-military entities as two of them were present in The Fleet led by the Battlestar Galactica.

The EVAC Raptor was Raptor Mk. IIIb multipurpose spacecraft used by Colonial first responders. It is a demilitarized version of the massively successful craft used by the Colonial Fleet and deployed since the First War.

The Gemenon Liner 1701-type civilian cruiser was a class of passenger liner operated by several airlines throughout the Cyrannus Star System, in the interwar period. Described as "fish-shaped", these relatively common spaceships would usually carry anywhere from 450 to 1350 passengers. While described as having maximum carrying capacity of around 1000,

Gemenon Liner 1701 was a Gemenon Liner 1701-type civilian cruiser, in service of Gemenon Liners airline. At some point after the attack, the liner lost its main power, and was effectively drifting in space, alongside three other ships. Shortly after found by the Colonial One, the ship came under Cylon nuclear attack, forcing Captain Adama to trigger massive electromagnetic pulse, shorting out the nuclear warheads and causing massive DRADIS jamming, fooling Cylons into believing a nuclear detonation occurred. Soon after, all passengers from Gemenon Liner 1701 were transferred to the Colonial One and the ships departed the area.
The Galleon was a "great ship", that departed from Galleon Meadow on Kobol some 2000 years before the Fall of the Twelve Colonies., that carried Twelve Tribes to their new home, among the stars.

Intersun Luxury Liners was a spaceline based in the Twelve Colonies of Kobol. By the 58th BCH, it was already recognized as one of the leading passenger carriers, operating numerous ships, including several Colonial Heavy 798-type, and by 0 ACH, at least one Zephyr-type vessel.
Griffon X7 was a prototype long-range multi-mission ship that was to serve as a supplement to the relatively short-range Mark III Raptors.

The Executive Officer (XO) is the second-in-command aboard a Colonial Fleet ship, typically holding the rank of Colonel or Lieutenant Colonel. The XO is responsible for the day-to-day management of the ship’s crew and operations, ensuring that the Commanders orders are carried out efficiently. They oversee administrative functions, personnel discipline, and operational readiness, and serve as the key advisor to the Commander on all matters concerning the ship.

David Glen Larson (born 22 July 1974 in Santa Monica) is an actor and writer, who played "Baby Walker" in the "Greetings from Earth" episode of Battlestar Galactica 1978". He later appeared as one of the Super Scouts in Galactica 1980, appearing in The Super Scouts, The Super Scouts, Part 2, Spaceball, The Night the Cylons Landed, Part 1 and Space Croppers.

The Loki-type was a heavy cruiser that served as a fleet support ship in the Colonial Fleet during the Cylon War. This class would be assigned to larger fleets or battlestar groups as a lightly armed support ship for protection. As a Fleet Support Ship, the Loki-type was designed to transfer munition, goods, and spare parts to combat ships.

McConnell is a supply ship within the fleet. The ship was one of several that Commander Jack Fisk secretly raided and built up a personal stockpile of high valued goods which he traded within the fleet's black market.
Kiya was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Kara Nixal was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Mutem Wia was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Odysseus was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.

Unnamed Mayor was the Mayor of Caprica City in the 50s BCH. Following the bombing of a Mag-Lev train by the Soldiers of The One, the Mayor held a press conference over the findings of a GDD investigation.

Loki was a heavy cruiser that served the Colonial Fleet during the Cylon War. Name for the shape-changing Norse god of mischief, the Loki was distinguished by a three-part hull beneath a domed upper structure that terminated in a huge alligator head.
Jim Shield is the actor who played Lieutenant Cohen "Karma" Baker in the Battlestar Galactica episodes "Kobol's Last Gleaming, Part Ⅰ" and "Kobol's Last Gleaming, Part II".

Jupiter-class Point-Defence Battery was a multi-barrel KEW close-in-weapon used on the Jupiter-class battlestars. Depending on the period, the class would boast some 550 of these last-line-of-defense weapons.
Nehalennia was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as part of the ragtag fleet.

Katherine Cannon is an American actress known for playing "Vela" in the Battlestar Galactica 1978 episode, "The Lost Warrior".

John Pyper-Ferguson is the actor who played Captain Cole "Stinger" Taylor in the Battlestar Galactica episodes "Pegasus" and "Resurrection Ship, Part Ⅰ" and Tomas Vergis in several episodes of Caprica.

The Raptor Mk. IIIa was a multipurpose spacecraft used by the Colonial Fleet. The Raptor was heavily used by the Colonial Fleet, capable of performing a variety of actions. Raptors posses miniature FTL drives, which allowed a limited FTL capability. The standard crew size for a Raptor is two, with a Pilot and Electronic Countermeasure Officer, though space allows for dedicated co-pilot.
A pilot was an individual qualified to fly, and capable of flying, air and spacecraft. In any two or more man crew, a pilot would usually be accompanied by a navigator.

Resurrection Ship, Part Ⅰ is an episode of the TV series, Battlestar Galactica, and aired during the show's second season. In the episode, Admiral Helena Cain and Commander William Adama call a truce but plan to assassinate each other. The humans destroy a Cylon fleet that includes a resurrection ship. Cain and Adama both cancel their plots, but Gina escapes from the Pegasus brig and kills Cain.
Resurrection Ship, Part Ⅱ is an episode of the TV series, Battlestar Galactica, and aired during the show's second season.

Razor is a Straight-to-DVD film spin-off of the 2004 Battlestar Galactica series. It is informally considered a two-part opening to Season 4 by staff, including Ron D. Moore, though its narrative links are not direct. It focuses on the life of Major Kendra Shaw as XO of Pegasus under Commander Lee Adama, with significant flashback sequences to the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as well as the Cylon War. The film marked the first appearance of Cylon War-era Centurions outside of the Miniseries, which would later re-appear in Season 4, and had narrative ties into Season 4 with a scene focusing on Lieutenant Kara Thrace's destiny, effectively making Razor the opening to Season 4.

Scorpia Traveller was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. Over two weeks after the attack, Scorpia Traveller docked with Galactica, and a Number Five hid in a group of civilians leaving the ship to conduct a suicide bombing on Galactica.

Tauron Traveler‏‎ was a civilian ship which formed part of President Laura Roslin's refugee fleet. In the days following the Fall of the Twelve Colonies, its captain made plans to abandon the fleet, chased by a Cylon force, and make its own journey. On the urging of President Roslin, Galactica launched several Vipers to intimidate the captain to fold back in. The ships later participated in the presidential election, resulting in the colonization of New Caprica.
The Raider was the standard attack craft used by the Cylon Empire.

Pyxis was a Gemenon Liner 1701-type civilian cruiser which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a fleet led by Galactica. It was destroyed during a Cylon ambush in an Ionian Nebula when an out-of-control raider crashed into its sublight drive. The resulting explosion destroyed the ship and all of its 600 passengers onboard.
Swordfish was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in the refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Tarbadek was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in the refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.

Salpica was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election. Later, it housed Samuel Anders before he moved aboard the Galactica.
Sargon was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Rhadamanthys was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Picon Princess was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.

Picon 26 was a colonial ship that survived the initial Cylon attack during the Fall of the Twelve Colonies and later rendezvoused with President Roslin's refugee fleet. Her captain protested Roslin's decision to abandon the non-FLT-equipped ships just as the Cylons showed up to attack the convoy of vessels. Presumably, the ship had FTL capability and jumped with the fleet as ordered.

Rycon was a battlestar which served in the Colonial Fleet during the Thousand-Yahren War. Led by Commander Kronus, Rycon was the command ship for the Fourth Colonial Fleet. Rycon was likely destroyed in the final years of the war, as it was absent at the Battle of Cimtar.

Taba was a Borellian Nomen who was living in the Twelve Colonies of Man at the time of the Battle of Cimtar. Like the others, he resided on a ship shared by the majority if not the entire population of Borellian refugees.

The Raptor Mk. II was a multipurpose spacecraft used by the Colonial Fleet during the First Cylon War. The Raptor was heavily used by the Colonial Fleet, capable of performing a variety of missions, from SEAD (Suppression of Enemy Air Defenses) missions to simple transport runs.
The Raptor Mk. IIIb Heavy was a multipurpose spacecraft used by the Colonial Fleet. Modification of the Mark III, this variant carries heavy underslung armament and missile pods.
Petty Officer 1st Class was an enlisted rank used by the Colonial Fleet. Its equivalent in the Colonial Marine Corps is Staff Sergeant.
Peter-John Prinsloo is an actor who played Lieutenant Mei "Freaker" Firelli in the Battlestar Galactica episode "Pegasus", "Resurrection Ship, Part Ⅰ" and "Resurrection Ship, Part Ⅱ‎".
Ramses-class was type of warship utilized by the Colonial Fleet during the interwar period shortly before the Fall of the Twelve Colonies.

Ranger-class was a class of warship utilized by the Colonial Fleet during the interwar period shortly before the Fall of the Twelve Colonies. A single decommissioned ship of this class survived the fall, and joined the Galactica-led ragtag fleet.
Shuttle Mark I was a type of small craft used by the Colonial Fleet for the transport of personnel and cargo.

The Raptor Mk. IIIb was a multipurpose spacecraft used by the Colonial Fleet. The Raptor was heavily used by the Colonial Fleet, capable of performing a variety of actions. Raptors posses miniature FTL drives, which allowed a limited FTL capability. The standard crew size for a Raptor is two, with a Pilot and Electronic Countermeasure Officer, though space allows for dedicated co-pilot.

The Raptor Mk. I was a multipurpose spacecraft used by the Colonial Fleet during the First Cylon War, capable of performing a variety of missions, from SEAD (Suppression of Enemy Air Defenses) missions to simple transport runs.
Polly Walker is the actress who played "Clarice Willow" in Caprica.

Zephyr was a Intersun Liners luxury liner which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a ragtag fleet led by Galactica. Zephyr was the largest civilian ship that survived and a ship with the largest number of survivors, including the Galactica and Pegasus.

The Viper Mk. VIIa was a space-superiority fighter used by the Colonial Fleet in the years prior to the Fall of the Twelve Colonies. It was the seventh generation of Viper, a series of fighters which had been in production since before the Cylon War.

The Viper is a series of superiority fighters, originally developed on Caprica, at least a decade before the Cylon War. Originally an air superiority fighter, by the time of Viper Mk. I, it grew into a space superiority fighter used by the Colonial Fleet.

The Viper Mk. II was the second generation of Viper space-superiority fighter used by the Colonial Fleet. The Mark II was used for much of the Cylon War, and while it was in the process of being replaced by the newer Mark III ten years in, it continued to see service at the war's conclusion.After the war, many Mark IIs were removed from service and scrapped, though a squadron's worth were tracked down and refitted in time for Galacticas decommissioning ceremony. Due to the lack of CNP and networking, the Mark IIs were immune to Cylon hacking, and these museum exhibits were made operational once more.

The Valkyrie-class battlestar was a type of warship that was operated by the individual Colonies before unification, and subsequently, the Colonial Fleet.Alongside the Artemis-class, they were one of the oldest known classes of battlestars. She is much smaller than the Jupiter-class and is believed to have been used as a light strike and reconnaissance ship. The Valkyrie-class was first deployed during the Cylon War and has proven to be very versatile, with many ships remaining in active service up until the Fall of the Twelve Colonies. The class spawned at least one significant refit, which remove a spoiler-like structure on its upper engine assembly.

The Gun on Ice Planet Zero is the sixth episode of Battlestar Galactica. It premiered on October 22, 1978. In syndication and on streaming, "The Gun on Ice Planet Zero" is sometimes listed as the eighth episode of the season. This happens when the series premiere episode, "Saga of a Star World", is split into three episodes.

The Gun on Ice Planet Zero: Part Ⅱ is the seventh episode of Battlestar Galactica. It premiered on October 29, 1978. In syndication and on streaming, "The Gun on Ice Planet Zero, Part Ⅱ" is sometimes listed as the ninth episode of the season. This happens when the series premiere episode, "Saga of a Star World", is split into three episodes.
Wilkens was the captain of the Astral Queen, a Colonial prison transport ship which joined The Fleet following the Fall of the Twelve Colonies.

Turbines are a type of Colonial light-aircraft constructed at the end of the fleet's journey to Earth. They were engineered for the use of Warrior teams sent to infiltrate Earth's society, and so appeared outwardly to be motorcycles, with the additional feature of deployable wings for flying. They were also built with nuclear field generators, which could camouflage them at the expense of significant power.
Ziusudra was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a ragtag fleet led by Galactica.

Thera Sita was a civilian SCT-type shuttle that survived the Fall of the Twelve Colonies and became part of the ragtag fleet led by the Galactica. The ship was first mentioned shortly before the fleet colonized New Caprica, participating in the presidential elections. After successfully surviving transit through the passage, some of the ship's passengers contracted Mellorak infection and had to be transferred to Dogsville, a make-shift civilian habitat on board the Galactica to receive medical care.
Tora Bashiri was a civilian ship which escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Vena Capa was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.
Virga was a civilian ship that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies in a refugee fleet. It took part in the presidential election.

The Viper Mk. VIIb was a space-superiority fighter used by the Colonial Fleet in the years prior to the Fall of the Twelve Colonies. It was the seventh generation of Viper, a series of fighters that had been in production since before the Cylon War. The Mark VIIb is an evolution of the Mark VIIa variant, featuring several design changes, most notably a more oval nose.
The main infobox used in pages about TV Shows & Movies is "Infobox Ship".

The Virgon Express-type is a flattop maintenance vessel class that was part of the ragtag fleet. A ship of this class was one of the first ships discovered by President Laura Roslin's Colonial One, alongside Gemenon Liner 1701, an SCT-type shuttle and a Monarch-type mining vessel.
Tiger-type was type of warship utilized by the Colonial Fleet during the interwar period shortly before the Fall of the Twelve Colonies.
The Zodiac-type battlestar was a type of warship utilized by the Colonial Fleet during the interwar period shortly before the Fall of the Twelve Colonies.

Valkyrie-class Point-Defence Battery was a dual-barrel KEW close-in-weapon used on the Valkyrie-class battlestars. Depending on the period, the class would boast some 30 of these last-line-of-defense weapons.

Unknown Ship was a civilian vessel that escaped the Fall of the Twelve Colonies as part of a civilian fleet later encountered by the Battlestar Pegasus. Like the other ships in the fleet, it was likely stripped of all valuable equipment and personnel, leaving it stranded in deep space.

Ship alerts on Colonial warships are known as action stations and are given to prepare the crews for battle. The alerts are typically by voice as well as by a klaxon in the following format: :"Action stations, action stations. Set condition one throughout the ship. This is not a drill." The three states of readiness are: :Condition One: Attack is present, or imminent. This alert places the ship at its highest state of readiness. All crews go to their combat posts. Bulkhead doors are closed in case of decompression. Additional Viper pilots are scrambled to supplement the Combat Air Patrol and the Alert Fighters, and flight support crews man their stations. The CIC is locked down and the ship's commander is on station. :Condition Two: Threat probable, but not present. Crew readiness is somewhat more relaxed than full readiness. This is usually ordered directly after the end of a Condition One alert. :Condition Three: This is the "all clear" alert, returning crews to their normal, day-to-day non-combat duties after Conditions One or Two. This is normal cruising during wartime. Weapons are partially manned, but the ship is at less than full readiness.

Agro-3 is an Agro Ship within the Fleet, along with its sister ship, Agro-2. The ship is essentially an enormous greenhouse floating in space, with the ship's primary bulk dedicated to soil deposits where plant life is cultivated for food. The remaining space is allocated to basic ship requirements, including a control center, engine room, and crew quarters. A vast transparent shell covers the garden areas, its many panes absorbing and storing stellar light, which radiates down upon the cultivated areas in alternating patches of illumination. This makes viewing the stars from inside the agro-ship difficult, though the stellar projectors provide warmth throughout the vessel.

Adena is a passenger ship within the known for its complement of socialators. Following the destruction of , Adena is converted into a forge ship, responsible for manufacturing new s and other critical military hardware for the Fleet.
Agro-2 is an Agro Ship within the Fleet that is destroyed during the battle with the Chitain.

Auxiliary Fire Control is located in the forward section of . This area likely allows the battlestar's gun batteries or missile launchers to be fired in the event that CIC cannot control these functions or if the command crew is incapacitated. Cylon Centurion forces infiltrating battlestars are reputed to use a tactic wherein their boarding parties take control of Auxiliary Fire Control, as well as Aft Damage Control. The Cylons in Aft Damage Control (which is able to coordinate bulkheads, vents, and firefighting throughout the ship) will attempt to vent the ship's atmosphere into space, asphyxiating the crew. Then, with no further hindrance, the Cylons in Auxiliary Fire Control would turn a battlestar's gun batteries at other Colonial ships to destroy them. Colonel Saul Tigh recalls this tactic while Galactica is boarded by advanced Centurion models, delivered by a Heavy Raider that managed to crash-land in the starboard flight pod landing bay during Galactica battle with a basestar . Tigh learns of this ploy from William Adama, as he recalled a similar attempt by Cylons that invaded Galactica while he was stationed there in the last week of the Cylon War some 40 years earlier (deleted scene, "Valley of Darkness"). To combat the Cylons, Tigh (in command of Galactica after Commander Adama is shot by Sharon Valerii) orders teams to stop the boarders from reaching these key control areas at all costs. Asha Janik, a colonist from Picon, is a member of the "Demand Peace" movement. Formerly a maintenance worker on a civilian ship in the Fleet, the Greenleaf, Janik is recruited to aid in ammunition creation and stocking for s. She apparently tampers with several rounds, leaving the casings weak and prone to explode, damaging a Viper's gun or even a whole wing section. One of her sabotaged rounds damages 's port gun during the start of her CAP duty shift. Chief Tyrol quickly identifies the problem as sabotage by weighing the rounds by hand and by memory. Captain Adama arrests her. Janik practically confesses to the crime when seeing Adama by yelling a declaration of her group's causes throughout the ammo machinery area as she's carted away. Later, Admiral Adama and Colonel Tigh look at brochures made by the "Demand Peace" movement that were found in Janik's quarters .

Atmospheric shuttles are smaller vessels employed by the Colonials for ship to ship, ship to planet, and planet to ship transport. There are at least two different models, with one dating back to the First Cylon War . After the Fall of the Twelve Colonies, these craft were quite popular in the surviving fleet for ship to ship travel, and often created busy space lanes which were easy to get lost in .

Airlocks serve as the entrance and exits to spaceships, whether it is docking with another ship or for extravehicular activity (EVA), without compromising the atmosphere of a spaceship. They consist of a hyperbaric chamber with a pair of airtight doors, one allowing access to the ship's interior and the other to the vacuum of space. The chamber can be pressurized and depressurized in a controlled fashion. A Viper launch tube constitutes a form of airlock with additional features for the rapid deployment of Vipers. Airlocks obtain notoriety as a method of execution, particularly following the Fall of the Twelve Colonies.

The anti-gravity ship is a singularly unique Colonial spacecraft, designed and built under the guidance of Doctor Zee, incorporating technological innovations far more advanced than either Cylon technology or conventional Colonial technology. Adama believes the vessel to be so powerful that, in sufficient numbers, a force of these vessels could actually enable the humans to retake the , but there are no further resources or raw materials to enable the Galactican Fleet to construct additional ships like it . The ship itself is unlike previous Colonial craft in both its saucer design and its oddly luminous nature, in addition to its capability of landing vertically. The ship also creates a mist upon entering Earth's atmosphere that can, when properly implemented, create rain clouds interspersed with nutrients to accelerate plant growth . The ship has the ability to analyze every facet of its surroundings, including the people who occupy such surroundings, and is capable of giving an accurate, detailed projection of what will happen in a period of time. In addition, the craft has advanced medical facilities. A curious bi-product of the ship is its ability to neutralize Earth's vehicles within roughly one mile of its landing zone. The vehicles part of Sydell's motorcade were neutralized as they approached the mountain, where the ship had landed . Alan J. Levi is the director of "Saga of a Star World" (for which he never was officially credited) and "The Gun on Ice Planet Zero" two-parter. Levi has directed other genre television, including Buffy the Vampire Slayer, 1976-77's Bionic Woman, The Incredible Hulk, and Quantum Leap.

Atreus is a member of the Tauron crime syndicate Ha'la'tha in the years prior to the Cylon War. Atreus and his men claim the gun trade in Caprica City, operating independently of the Guatrau. Some fifty-eight years before the Fall of the Twelve Colonies, Atreus and his men take reprisal on Sam Adama when Adama threatens their trade by shipping weapons to aid in the second Tauron Uprising. Atreus shoots and kills Adama's cohort, Demos, but allows Adama to live, confiscating his weapons and giving him a message for the Guatrau. Later, as Atreus and his men celebrate at the Skybar, a U-87 soldier robot under the control of Adama storms the club and opens fire, killing Atreus and his men . de: Atreus

Autogyros are small rotary wing aircraft that patrol the skies of V-world's New Cap City. Launched from the formidable Dreadnaught, these single-pilot rotorcraft strafe the streets of New Cap City, drezzing users . New Cap City gamer Tad "Heracles" Thorean was a victim of an autogyro attack during his attempt to help Joseph Adama locate his deceased daughter Tamara Adama, lost in V-world .

The Air Force Viper is a Caprican Air Force aircraft used for atmospheric flight on in the years prior to the Cylon War. It follows an earlier model and predates those Vipers used by the Colonial Fleet in the first and second Cylon engagements. A Viper flight simulator featuring these single-pilot fighter jets is available through the virtual world interface for holoband users. Fifty-eight years before the Fall of the Twelve Colonies, Zoe Graystone and her date Philomon fly atmospheric Vipers over a simulated sea and oil rigs. Unfamiliar with the controls, Zoe accidentally collides with Philomon's fighter, sending both jets crashing into the water .
Ariadna is a civilian pleasure liner of the . In the aftermath of the , the ship holds eight hundred refugees fleeing the Cylon tyranny in the .

The battle for the Delphi occurs as a result of the ship loosing its place in the Fleet due to engine trouble. As predicted by Doctor Zee, the Cylons are able to find the ship and begin their attack. Immediately prior to this, Commander Adama orders Colonel Boomer to launch a Viper escort, particularly as the ship contains all the Fleet's children. As the ship is attacked, Warriors Troy and Dillon aid the ship's civilian crew in evacuating the children to shuttles. Meanwhile, a team lead by Colonel Boomer himself tackle the Raiders, but the ship is already in its death throes. The Cylons break off their attack once the ship is effectively mortally wounded, but all who were aboard apparently escape .
Big Spud is the nickname or "wireless code name" used by the Colonials for a large asteroid in the same field that the mining ship Majahual found an asteroid with extensive ore deposits .

"Bingo" (or "bingo fuel") is Viper pilot slang that indicates that their fighter's fuel reserves are too low to continue their mission and have the minimum amount of fuel necessary to return to their battlestar before running out. A pilot usually makes the declaration to their wingman, CAG or battlestar by shouting "bingo fuel!". A Viper that's out of fuel is virtually impossible to fly, yet manages to do so after she is involved with an in-flight accident that severs her fuel line . The term can also be jokingly used to indicate that one is out of alcohol .

Battlestar Galactica Deadlock, see: Berzerk (Deadlock). Berzerk is a support ship in service with the Colonial Fleet sometime prior to the Fall of the Twelve Colonies. The ship was docked near the battlestar (BS 62) at the Scorpion Fleet Shipyards when the Cylons struck as part of their attack on the Colonies. It is destroyed by multiple Raider squadrons after the Cylons shut down the ship's systems by exploiting a backdoor in the Command Navigation Program .
The Battlestar Galactica Galactic Cruiser is an toy produced by Larami Corp. According to the package, it features "NON-TOXIC PAINT," "STURDY CONSTRUCTION," and "FREE ROLLING".

The Berzerk type cruiser was a battlestar group support vessel in service with the Colonial Fleet since the First Cylon War. These vessels serve as support to their respective battlestar groups, where two or three can be assigned at a time .

The Blackhawk is a twin-engine VTOL aircraft employed by the Caprican Marine Corps in the years prior to the First Cylon War. Fifty-eight years before the Fall of the Twelve Colonies, the Caprican Marines dispatch one of these aircraft to pursue an escaped Cylon prototype from Graystone Industries, alongside a Caprican Air Force Phoenix-type jet . Some months later, a squadron of U-87 Cyber Combat Units operate several Marine Blackhawks in an assault on Soldiers of the One terrorists, landing on the field of Atlas Arena and engaging the attackers in a firefight . These vehicles employ DRADIS technology .

Battlestar Galactica Deadlock: Modern Ship Pack is the final expansion for the Battlestar Galactica Deadlock game, featuring added content in terms of ships, weapons, and other pertinent updates. Its release is part of the "Season 2" package for the game series.
__NOTOC__ A brig is a compartment that serves as a detention space aboard a ship. Persons confined to the brig are informally said to be "in hack" .

Cami is a young girl onboard the sublight civilian spacecraft called the Botanical Cruiser. At the time of the Cylon Attack, she is travelling with her grandparents, but her grandmother succumbs to unspecified health problems. In her grandmother's stead, the captain of the Botanical Cruiser and his staff look after the child. During Laura Roslin's visit, Cami talks to new president about reuniting with her parents on , having chicken pot pie, and other things she looked forward to on her return home, innocently oblivious to the holocaust and the peril she was thrust in. Unable to be evacuated in time, the young girl is subsequently killed when a Cylon task force destroys her ship, while the FTL-capable ships jumped to Ragnar Anchorage to rendevous with Commander William Adama's .

Bow is a new pilot recruit who is left in command of Cadets Cree and Shields. He is the first to notice a flash of light emanating off Arcta's surface, and is in striking range of the Ravashol pulsar when it kills him. He is only the first of a few casualties of the weapons-deployed Pulsar .

Carmichael is the Lead Agro Specialist on board Agro Ship 9. Carmichael informs that, in order to procure food to feed , they would need to obtain new seeds of a variety of edible agro plants . He is also present when Count Iblis "miraculously" manages to grow large amounts of edible food on the agro ship. Like the rest of the Fleet, he is lead to believe that this is a "miracle" from Iblis, however it turns out to be just another trick to take the Fleet on a journey of his own evils . Carmichael observes Iblis kissing Sheba in the ship's gardens, and quickly walks away to avoid being noticed . de: Carmichael

CBDR is an acronym for Constant Bearing, Decreasing Range, and refers to an object on an intercept (or collision) course with a ship. Raiders on attack approach to can be CBDR . When Pegasus first appears on DRADIS, Lieutenant Gaeta indicates the DRADIS target as CBDR to Galactica .

Briton is a pilot on patrol with Captain Kanon when a specialized Raider appears. Unable to destroy the Raider with lasers, Kanon rams the enemy fighter with his Viper, disabling the Raider and injuring Briton in the process. Their Viper is considered missing for some time until it manages to limp back to to warn them of the humanoid Cylons detected onboard the stricken Raider . de:Briton

The Caprica City Medical Center is a medical care facility on Caprica. Gaius Baltar is treated here by Simon after a hit-and-run car accident in the Red Light District. Britt-Marie Eklund (born October 6, 1942, Stockholm, Sweden) is a Swedish actress who played Tenna in "The Gun on Ice Planet Zero, Part I" and "Part II". Ekland established herself as one of the most photographed actresses of the 1970s through her roles in Get Carter (1971), the cult horror film The Wicker Man (1973), and as Bond girl Mary Goodnight in The Man with the Golden Gun (1974).

Broadside is a supply ship within the Fleet, commanded by Captain Ironhand (Stedonis). Once an intergalactic shuttle serving the Twelve Worlds, it has been repurposed as a cargo vessel and serves as a refuge for outcasts and fugitives within the Fleet.

Cerebus is a civilian ship serving as the archive vessel within the Colonial Fleet. Cerebus serves the fleet in a specialized capacity, housing the archives and historical records of the Twelve Colonies. The ship is positioned among the other civilian vessels in the middle section of the fleet, visible alongside notable ships such as the Delphi, a marketplace freighter, and the Adena, a passenger liner.
Chitain ships are the vessels employed by the Chitain race, biomechanical craft that mirror the physical characteristics of their builders.

Reconnaissance drones (shortened in common parlance to recon drone) are deployed as part of the armament on basestars. The exterior appearance of the craft probably has not changed greatly over time since the Cylon War, as two detachments of them are easily identified by Lieutenant Kara "Starbuck" Thrace while reconnoitering the upper limits of the atmosphere of Ragnar while re-arms herself at Ragnar Anchorage .
